statement: For finite FK with arbitrary boundary partition, 0<p<1, q>=1 and pairwise disjoint nonempty edge sets C_i, P(all C_i have an open edge)<=product_i[1-(1-p)^|C_i|].
source_quote: The same bound holds after conditioning on any positive-probability event measurable without e
why: Independently rederived the full conditional formula p or p/(p+q(1-p)); tower conditioning preserves closed>=1-p. Every prefix event is measurable outside the next C_i, so the chain rule is valid. No independence is used. Exact controls below show the assumptions matter.
remaining_gap: None identified in this scoped inequality; this is not the parent critical-ordering lower bound.

statement: For G=Z Cartesian-product H with finite connected H of m vertices, q>=1 and p<1, ordinary crossing probabilities are bounded by [1-(1-p)^m]^n; all ordinary infinite clusters are absent. Integer-q color-boundary magnetization vanishes at every finite beta.
assumptions: cuts contained in the finite volume
source_quote: all ordinary open clusters are finite for every p<1
why: Each physical path must cross every longitudinal cut; the pairwise disjoint cutsets permit L1. An infinite cluster leaves each finite interval, giving the two-end union bound. Wired identifications do not create an ordinary crossing. Edwards-Sokal boundary connection is an ordinary path to at least one physical end.
remaining_gap: No claim of free-energy analyticity or of behavior on Z^3 is being audited.

statement: Z Cartesian-product K5 is simple, connected, transitive, six-regular and amenable, but its q=3 Potts model has no finite-temperature spontaneous magnetization.
assumptions: the graph is Z x K5, not Z^3
source_quote: This refutes the stronger hypothetical bridge
why: Degree is 2+4=6; interval fibers have 5(2n+1) vertices and 10 outgoing edges. L2 applies. The example fails pc<1 and has linear growth, so it does not refute bridges with those additional hypotheses or the original target.
remaining_gap: Critical wired ordering on the actual Z^3 lattice remains unproved.
